note: Pilot pool candidates for the permutations page (Mirrored/Rotated/Swapped slots). Regenerated 2026-07-16 after the original generating session lost its step data (context-only, never persisted). Step data below is captured verbatim from MCP generate_sequence responses; prose is verified against THESE instances step-by-step. Loop-closure lesson: the engine's random start draw can pick position pairs invalid for the requested loopType and error out. When that happens, probe validate_loop_options and force startPlacement/endPlacement.

candidates.prose: In GΘSZ, every rotation in the first half is clockwise. The mirrored half repeats the same letters counter-clockwise. The left hand rests on Θ and Z, so you can watch the right hand's direction flip at the seam.
candidates.proseNote: Colors swapped vs the first draft: this instance rests BLUE on Θ/Z (steps 2,4,6,8 blue static) while red moves every step.
verified: steps 1-4: every moving rotation cw
steps 5-8: every moving rotation ccw
blue static on both Θ steps (2,6) and both Z steps (4,8)
red moves on all 8 steps; direction flips cw→ccw at the seam

candidates.prose: ZDCΣ travels through all three position families: gamma, beta, alpha. Its reflection walks the mirrored path with every rotation direction inverted.
candidates.proseNote: One word changed from first draft ('retraces the same path' → 'walks the mirrored path'): the second half visits mirrored positions (alpha7 vs alpha3), not identical ones.
verified: positions visit gamma (gamma1, gamma9), beta (beta1), alpha (alpha3, alpha1, alpha7)
every rotation direction inverted in second half (blue ccw→cw on all steps, red cw→ccw on D and C)

candidates.prose: W-BLΘ opens each half with a dash: the right hand cuts straight across while the left circles. The mirror survives a Type 3 letter unchanged.
candidates.proseNote: Weakest of the three per first-round ranking; keep only if a dash should be represented in this slot.
verified: step 1 and step 5 are both W- with a red dash
second half inverts every blue/red rotation direction (ccw→cw)

candidates.prose: JΘZΦ opens with the hands circling in opposite directions at once. The mirrored half flips both: whatever ran clockwise comes back counter-clockwise, down to the closing Φ dash.
verified: step 1 (J): blue ccw and red cw simultaneously: split directions
steps 5-8 invert every rotation direction from steps 1-4
red finishes its work on J and Θ, then rests through Z and Φ in both halves

candidates.prose: This 4-letter word repeats rotated 180°. The left hand circles counter-clockwise the whole way through (it never changes direction) while the right hand answers clockwise on every other step and rests between.
candidates.proseNote: Colors and directions swapped vs the first draft: this instance runs BLUE ccw on all 8 steps; red moves cw on odd steps only.
verified: blue rotates ccw on every step 1-8, never flipping
red moves cw on steps 1,3,5,7 and is static on 2,4,6,8
half-slice lands 180° around (alpha7 → alpha3), home on step 8

candidates.proseNote: Structurally the same lesson as the DΨ default (2-step slice, Ψ-family, 90°): fair alternate, low variety. Keep or cut on that basis.

all positions in the beta family; I alternates with the Ψ- dash-dash step

candidates.prose: Δ-RΛY repeats rotated 180°. Nothing flips. Every rotation in both halves runs clockwise, and the pattern simply picks itself up and lands halfway around the grid.
candidates.proseNote: Pedagogically strong pairing with the mirrored slot: rotated preserves directions, mirrored inverts them.
verified: every moving rotation on all 8 steps is cw (dashes and statics carry no rotation)
second half repeats the letters with positions carried around: beta5 start → beta1 half-way → beta5 home

candidates.prose: XΣ repeats rotated 90°. The hands strictly alternate: right moves on every X while left holds, and left answers on every Σ. Each two-step slice sets the pattern down a quarter of the way around.
verified: perfect alternation: X steps move red only (anti cw), Σ steps move blue only (pro ccw)
red's direction is always cw, blue's always ccw, across all four slices
four 2-step slices, home at gamma15 on step 8

candidates.prose: In ΔZΩX, only one hand moves at a time. The second repetition trades parts: every motion the left hand played, the right hand takes, and the resting hand answers. Each motion is an anti-spin.
verified: exactly one hand moves on every step 1-8
every moving motion is anti
steps 5-8 trade colors with steps 1-4 (blue's Δ,Z go to red; red's Ω,X go to blue)

candidates.prose: UYFΘ- keeps both hands moving. At the halfway point they trade parts: the left hand picks up exactly what the right played on step one, and the right takes the left's.
verified: both hands move on steps 1,3,4,5,7,8 (one static each on 2 and 6 only)
step 5 blue (pro ccw) = step 1 red; step 5 red (anti cw) = step 1 blue

candidates.prose: In RY-GΣ-, every rotation runs clockwise from start to finish. What trades is the dash: the left hand cuts across on the first pass, and on the repeat the right hand takes the cut.
verified: every moving rotation on all 8 steps is cw
first-half dashes: blue on Y- (step 2), red on Σ- (step 4); second half trades them (red step 6, blue step 8)
step 5 trades step 1's parts (blue anti cw ↔ red pro cw)

dash ownership: red on steps 1-3, blue on 4; traded in the second half (blue 5-7, red 8)
